things-fall-apart.title: Things Fall Apart
things-fall-apart.author: Chinua Achebe
things-fall-apart.summary: Okonkwo, a respected Igbo warrior, struggles to protect his status and way of life as personal choices and colonial change transform his community.
things-fall-apart.why: A landmark African novel that centres Igbo society and examines authority, culture, family and colonial disruption.

no-longer-at-ease.title: No Longer at Ease
no-longer-at-ease.author: Chinua Achebe
no-longer-at-ease.summary: Obi Okonkwo returns to Nigeria after studying abroad and finds his ideals tested by family obligations, money, status and corruption.
no-longer-at-ease.why: It explores the pressures facing an educated Nigerian caught between inherited obligations and a changing colonial order.

arrow-of-god.title: Arrow of God
arrow-of-god.author: Chinua Achebe
arrow-of-god.summary: Chief priest Ezeulu tries to defend spiritual authority as rivalry and British colonial influence reshape his community.
arrow-of-god.why: The novel studies the fragility of political and spiritual power when internal conflict meets colonial pressure.

purple-hibiscus.title: Purple Hibiscus
purple-hibiscus.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
purple-hibiscus.summary: Teenager Kambili grows up in a wealthy but tightly controlled household and gradually encounters a freer way of living through her aunt and cousins.
purple-hibiscus.why: A family story about authority, faith, silence and a young girl's discovery of voice and freedom.

half-of-a-yellow-sun.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
half-of-a-yellow-sun.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
half-of-a-yellow-sun.summary: Intertwined lives are transformed by the creation of Biafra and the Nigerian Civil War as love, loyalty and survival collide.
half-of-a-yellow-sun.why: It combines intimate relationships with a major episode of African history and shows war through ordinary human lives.

americanah.title: Americanah
americanah.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
americanah.summary: Ifemelu and Obinze leave Nigeria on different paths abroad, then confront what migration has changed when they return to a transformed home.
americanah.why: The novel connects migration, race, class, romance and the changing meaning of belonging.

dream-count.title: Dream Count
dream-count.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
dream-count.summary: Four women's lives intersect across Nigeria and the United States through love, ambition, motherhood, friendship and self-examination.
dream-count.why: A contemporary exploration of women's inner lives and the distance between imagined and lived futures.

weep-not-child.title: Weep Not, Child
weep-not-child.author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
weep-not-child.summary: Njoroge believes education can secure a better future, but his family is drawn into the violence surrounding the Mau Mau uprising and British colonial rule.
weep-not-child.why: It shows how political conflict reshapes childhood, family loyalty and hope.

a-grain-of-wheat.title: A Grain of Wheat
a-grain-of-wheat.author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
a-grain-of-wheat.summary: As a village prepares to celebrate Kenyan independence, private secrets and betrayals complicate the public story of resistance and heroism.
a-grain-of-wheat.why: The novel questions simple ideas of heroes and traitors by showing the moral cost of liberation struggles.

petals-of-blood.title: Petals of Blood
petals-of-blood.author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
petals-of-blood.summary: A murder investigation frames the transformation of Ilmorog as development, commerce and inequality reshape the lives of its people.
petals-of-blood.why: A critique of post-independence inequality and the broken promises of national development.

kintu.title: Kintu
kintu.author: Jennifer Nansubuga Makumbi
kintu.summary: Beginning in the Buganda Kingdom, the story follows a family across generations as a curse links the distant past to contemporary Uganda.
kintu.why: A major Ugandan family saga blending history, mythology, Ganda storytelling and questions of inheritance.

manchester-happened.title: Manchester Happened
manchester-happened.author: Jennifer Nansubuga Makumbi
manchester-happened.summary: Stories move between Uganda and Britain as migrants leave, return, remember and renegotiate what home means.
manchester-happened.why: A nuanced portrait of migration, family, language and belonging between Uganda and Britain.

the-first-woman.title: The First Woman
the-first-woman.author: Jennifer Nansubuga Makumbi
the-first-woman.summary: Kirabo grows up asking questions about her absent mother and about womanhood while family secrets, folklore and friendship shape her identity.
the-first-woman.why: A Ugandan coming-of-age story that combines history, storytelling traditions and questions about gender and power.

waiting.title: Waiting
waiting.author: Goretti Kyomuhendo
waiting.summary: During the final period of Idi Amin's rule, teenager Alinda and her family confront violence, displacement and uncertainty in rural Uganda.
waiting.why: National political violence is shown through the everyday experience of a young woman and her family.

whispers-from-vera.title: Whispers from Vera
whispers-from-vera.author: Goretti Kyomuhendo
whispers-from-vera.summary: Vera, an ambitious professional woman in Kampala, tries to balance love, marriage, family expectations and career as a relationship forces difficult choices.
whispers-from-vera.why: A lively portrait of urban Ugandan womanhood, relationships and independence.

promises.title: Promises
promises.author: Goretti Kyomuhendo
promises.summary: A young Ugandan couple is separated by migration and financial pressure, testing loyalty, hope and the promises they make to one another.
promises.why: A contemporary story about migration, family life, separation and survival.

tropical-fish.title: Tropical Fish
tropical-fish.author: Doreen Baingana
tropical-fish.summary: Christine Mugisha and her sisters move through adolescence, faith, relationships, loss and migration between Uganda and the United States.
tropical-fish.why: An intimate coming-of-age portrait of Ugandan girls and women and the complicated meaning of home.

native-life-in-south-africa.title: Native Life in South Africa
native-life-in-south-africa.author: Sol T. Plaatje
native-life-in-south-africa.summary: Sol Plaatje documents the effects of the 1913 Natives' Land Act on Black South Africans, combining firsthand observation, political argument and accounts of families displaced from their land.
native-life-in-south-africa.why: A major early work by a Black South African writer and political leader, preserving firsthand testimony about land dispossession and segregation.

interesting-narrative-olaudah-equiano.title: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano
interesting-narrative-olaudah-equiano.author: Olaudah Equiano
interesting-narrative-olaudah-equiano.summary: Equiano recounts his childhood in Africa, enslavement, travels across the Atlantic world, purchase of his freedom and later work as an abolitionist.
interesting-narrative-olaudah-equiano.why: One of the most influential first-person narratives connected to the African experience of the transatlantic slave trade and the abolition movement.

story-of-an-african-farm.title: The Story of an African Farm
story-of-an-african-farm.author: Olive Schreiner
story-of-an-african-farm.summary: Set on a Karoo farm, the novel follows Waldo, Em and Lyndall from childhood toward adulthood while questioning religion, gender expectations, love and personal freedom.
story-of-an-african-farm.why: An important early South African novel, especially noted for its challenge to Victorian assumptions about women, marriage and independence.
